title: Orsen and the Ember
premise: Orsen Pemberton survives in the memoryless valley of Hollowmere by stealing recollections from travelers and selling them to the Guild of Kept Things, trading on the fact that magic cannot cross the valley's borders. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Orsen realizes the girl is a living vessel of the Ember—the last spark of the war-magic that once burned the world—and that the Guild has been harvesting valley-stolen memories for decades to feed it. Hunted by her former employers, shadowed by a disgraced knight who owes her his life, and forced to choose between the found family she built among thieves and the truth the child carries, Orsen smuggles the girl out of the only safe place she has ever known. In the end, Orsen learns the Ember chooses its bearer: rather than let it reignite the ancient war or be devoured by the Guild, she takes the fire into herself, sacrificing her stolen memories—including every moment with the people she loves—to seal it, waking in a world where she must be loved without remembering why.
about_author: R. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed, an experience that left a lasting fascination with what people choose to remember and what they pay to forget. Zhou writes fantasy about outsiders carrying dangerous truths, and lives quietly somewhere with unreliable weather.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes Hollowmere, where magic dies at the border and memories fade like breath on glass. Orsen lifts a soldier's recollection of his daughter's face and sells it to the Guild, hating herself a little more each time. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness; we see how much she remembers for others because no one remembers for her.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Wrong Hour
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On a night when even thieves stay indoors, a small girl appears at Orsen's door, barefoot in snow, speaking a language that makes Orsen's stolen memories ache in recognition. The girl clutches a coal that never cools. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant tenderness—Orsen, who steals other people's pasts, is handed someone else's future.

chapters.title: What the Coal Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with fragments of the girl's visions. Touching the ember-coal floods Orsen with images of burning cities and a war fought with memory itself. She realizes the child isn't cursed—she's a container. Emotional beat: horror curdling into resolve; Orsen understands why the Guild pays so well for old memories.

chapters.title: The Guild of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She visits her handler, Master Corvane, to feel out what the Guild knows, and notices new wards being drawn around the vaults—and sketches of a child on the clerks' desks. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; the safe life was always a cage, and the bars are now visible.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Owed Her
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric's POV. A disgraced knight exiled to Hollowmere recalls how Orsen stole back his worst memory years ago and kept it instead of selling it—a debt he never repaid. He finds her watching the roads. Emotional beat: gruff loyalty offered; the first thread of found family beyond Orsen's solitary craft.

chapters.title: Thieves' Oath
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The girl—whom Orsen names Wren—has been traced. Guild enforcers search the tenements. Orsen calls in favors from the thief community: Fenna the lockwright, deaf twins Pim and Sable, old Mother Quill. Emotional beat: warmth under pressure; Orsen discovers she belongs to something after all.

chapters.title: The Language Beneath Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Mother Quill's POV. The oldest resident of Hollowmere recognizes fragments of Wren's speech from a book burned before she was born: it predates kingdoms, from the age when the Ember chose bearers and nations burned for them. Emotional beat: awe and grief; history is not dead here, only sleeping.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Master Corvane corners Orsen privately: give up the child and the Guild will make her rich, restore her own erased childhood—which she learns she sold willingly long ago. Emotional beat: temptation with teeth; Orsen confronts the hole where her identity should be.

chapters.title: Running the Border
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crew smuggles Wren toward the valley's edge, where magic cannot follow—but neither can safety, since the Ember's pursuers wait outside. A chase across the salt flats ends with Aldric holding the pass alone. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; leaving means becoming someone new.

chapters.title: Outside the Magicless Land
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered through sensation and image as her language begins surfacing in Orsen's mind. Beyond the border, the world hums with power, and Wren's coal burns brighter—every league reawakening the war-magic inside her. Emotional beat: wonder laced with fear; freedom and danger arrive together.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They travel the pilgrim road through land scarred by the ancient war, meeting refugees who whisper of Guild riders asking after a child. Fenna is taken in a night raid meant for Wren. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into anger; Orsen's choices now cost other people.

chapters.title: What Aldric Buried
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. He confesses he once served the Guild's outer circle and deserted after seeing what the vaults fed: the Ember, half-starved, kept alive on harvested memories. His disgrace was engineered to place him near the valley. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as redemption; loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: The City of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They reach Vaskarren, the Guild's capital, to trade information and free Fenna. Orsen walks its memory-markets again—but this time as prey, wearing another woman's recollections as a disguise. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; Orsen wears borrowed selves so well she nearly loses her own.

chapters.title: Fenna's Price
chapters.summary: Fenna's POV. Imprisoned in the vaults, Fenna endures memory-extraction and learns the Guild's plan: feed Wren's Ember with a nation's worth of stolen pasts and control the resulting god-fire. She leaves coded messages in her own extracted memories. Emotional beat: defiance in captivity; even emptied, she resists.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Ledger Hall
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Using Fenna's codes and Pim and Sable's hands, the crew breaches the vaults and finds rows of memory-jars—and Corvane waiting, holding Orsen's original childhood in a jar labeled with her true name. Emotional beat: devastating choice; everything she was sits within arm's reach.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Corvane offers the jar: her erased childhood in exchange for Wren. Orsen opens it, receives one memory—her mother's voice singing—and shatters the rest, choosing the self she built over the self that was taken. Emotional beat: heartbreak as liberation; identity is chosen, not recovered.

chapters.title: Ember Unbound
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The rescue triggers the vault's harvest; the Ember tears partially free of Wren, and the Guild's stored memories ignite into a storm of ghost-voices. Wren, terrified, begs Orsen to take it before it becomes a weapon. Emotional beat: climax ignition; the child asks the thief to steal the one thing that cannot be carried lightly.

chapters.title: The Taking
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax. Orsen accepts the Ember into herself, and it begins consuming her memories as fuel—she fights Corvane while forgetting him mid-struggle, forgets Aldric's name, forgets the valley, holding on only to the decision itself. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full burn; love persisting after its memories are gone.

chapters.title: Ash and Quiet
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Ember, sealed in Orsen, goes dormant; the vault collapses; Corvane dies clutching jars of other people's yesterdays. Aldric carries the unconscious Orsen and silent Wren out of ruined Vaskarren. Emotional beat: exhausted aftermath; survival feels less like victory than a debt to the living.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Speaks Now
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With the Ember quieted, Wren's own voice returns—her first spoken words are Orsen's name, though Orsen no longer knows whose it is. Wren resolves to become the keeper of Orsen's story, telling it back to her piece by piece. Emotional beat: tender reversal; the saved child becomes the savior's memory.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating briefly among Aldric, Fenna, Pim, and Sable. The crew resettles at the valley's edge, building a home for a woman who doesn't know why they love her but lets them anyway. Small rituals: retelling shared stories, keeping her favorite foods stocked. Emotional beat: bittersweet domesticity; found family rebuilt around absence.

chapters.title: The First New Memory
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Watching snow fall on the rebuilt house, Orsen—who can no longer remember anything she stole or lost—makes a deliberate first memory: Wren laughing, Aldric mending the fence, Fenna swearing at a stubborn lock. She doesn't know her past, but she chooses this future. Emotional beat: quiet hope; identity begins again, freely given this time.
